subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Continues the school Drive Quran folder progression (TPS Quran Tracker tajweed rules Years 1-6) into KS3/KS4; classical tajweed (Hafs 'an 'Asim) and tadabbur method; Qur'an text per the Madinah mushaf

lessons.title: Starting KS3: baseline recitation and goals
objectives: Recite known surahs for a baseline assessment
Use a tajweed rubric to judge a recitation
Set three goals for the year

keywords.def: a table of criteria used to judge quality

starter: Bismillah. Recite the isti'adha and basmalah.
Name the four rules of noon sakinah and tanween.
Name three kinds of madd and their counts.

teach.heading: Why we recite with care
teach.note: Begin with adab and the ayah meaning. Explain that KS3 builds precision: we move from knowing rules to applying them without thinking. Ask: how does a footballer practise basics?

teach.heading: The rubric
bullets: Makharij: letters from the right place
teach.note: Hand out a four-row rubric with levels 1-4. Pupils will use it each half term. Walk through one example row. Stress that it is a tool for growth, not for comparison.

teach.heading: Baseline recitation
bullets: Record or recite to the teacher
teach.note: Pupils recite in breakout rooms or one by one. Record where permitted. Listen for one strength and one target per pupil. Keep the mood supportive and calm.

teach.heading: Setting goals
teach.note: Pupils write SMART goals and share one. Link goals to a dua: Allah, make the Qur'an the spring of my heart. Keep to a modest, honest list.

practice: Name the three tanween sounds.
How many counts is natural madd?
independent: Complete a self-assessment using the rubric
Recite Al-Fatihah and Al-Ikhlas for baseline
Write three goals for the year
exit: Name two rows of the rubric.
Write one goal for this half term.
lessons.homework: Practise your first goal for five minutes each day and note progress in a log.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: rubric with icons and sentence stems for goals. Stretch: design a personal tracker.

lessons.title: Makharij 1: the jawf and the throat
objectives: Locate the jawf and three throat points
Say each throat letter from its point
Contrast throat letters accurately

keywords.def: the empty space of the mouth and throat for the madd letters

starter: Name the five areas of makharij.

teach.heading: 17 points in 5 areas
teach.note: Show the diagram of the 17 makharij. Pupils copy it. Explain that all letters come from these 17 points, which is a principle taught by scholars of tajweed. Ask: which area has the most?

teach.heading: The jawf
bullets: Home of ا و ي when they are madd letters
The sound flows through the open space
No tongue or lip stops it
teach.note: Pupils say a long aa, oo, ee and notice that nothing blocks the sound. Contrast with a short vowel. Explain that the madd letters are not letters from the tongue or lips.

teach.heading: The throat
teach.note: Say each pair with a vowel. Notice how the sound moves from deep to upper throat. Pupils place a hand on the throat and feel. Take care with ع: no strain.

teach.heading: Practice and contrast
teach.note: Pupils say each pair and decide which is deeper. Words: Fatihah الْحَمْدُ, Nas أَعُوذُ, Falaq غَاسِقٍ and خَلَقَ. Pair feedback with the rubric.

practice: Give an example of a throat letter from the deep throat.
What is special about the jawf?
independent: Label a diagram of the 17 points
Say 12 words, naming the throat point of each throat letter
Record yourself saying the six throat letters with fathah, kasrah, dammah
exit: How many makharij points are in the throat?
Name a middle-throat letter.
lessons.homework: Practise the six throat letters daily with three vowels and record yourself once.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: labelled diagram and audio. Stretch: explain the difference between ح and ه.

lessons.title: Makharij 2: the tongue
objectives: Name the ten tongue points
Say the letters from each point
Distinguish close tongue letters

teach.heading: Ten points on the tongue
teach.note: Show the tongue diagram. Teach the first four points: qaaf (the deepest), kaaf (a little forward), jeem-sheen-yaa from the middle, and Daad from the side. Pupils say each letter with fathah.

teach.heading: Tip of the tongue
bullets: ن - the tip with the gum
ط  د  ت - the tip with the base of the upper teeth
teach.note: Say noon and raa. Raa is not rolled. Say ط د ت and discuss the difference: Taa is heavy; daal and taa are light. Take care of raa: one touch, not a roll.

teach.heading: Between the teeth and whistling
bullets: ظ  ذ  ث - tip with the edge of the upper teeth
ص  ز  س - tip near the lower teeth, whistling
Contrast: ظ  ذ  ث  /  ص  ز  س
teach.note: Say the two groups. Pupils can see their tongue on camera. The whistling group has a clear 'ssss' sound. Take particular care with ظ and ذ.

teach.heading: Word practice
teach.note: Pupils read each word and name the points of the underlined letter. Take extra time with Daad: the side of the tongue meets the molars. Praise patient practice.

practice: Name the two letters from the back of the tongue.
Which letter comes from the side of the tongue?
independent: Match 18 tongue letters to the right point
Read 10 pairs of words with close letters
Record and review a list of eight words with your rubric
exit: Which three letters come from the middle of the tongue?
Say the whistling letters.
lessons.homework: Say the 18 tongue letters in order daily with fathah and check yourself in a mirror.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: tongue diagram with colour coding. Stretch: explain how to teach Daad to a friend.

lessons.title: Makharij 3: lips, nose and consolidation
objectives: Name the two lip points and the nasal point
Say lip letters accurately
Apply all 17 points in a word
starter: Name the five areas and give a letter for each.

teach.heading: The lips
bullets: ف - the upper teeth and the inside of the lower lip
teach.note: Say each letter. Pupils watch each other. Notice ب is a stop, م has ghunnah, و is rounded. Take care that ف is not b.

teach.heading: The nose
bullets: Idgham and ikhfa also use it
teach.note: Pupils hum and feel the vibration. Ask: which letters have ghunnah in their nature? Noon and meem. Remind pupils that two counts is the length.

teach.heading: Review all 17
bullets: Throat: ء ه ع ح غ خ
Lips and nose: ف ب م و, ghunnah
teach.note: Quick-fire: teacher says a letter; pupils name the point. Increase speed gradually. Use the diagram as support.

teach.heading: Apply in a surah
bullets: Name the point for each letter
teach.note: Take Al-Falaq ayah 1 and label letters with their points. Pupils recite with attention to each letter. Give feedback from the rubric.

practice: Which letters come from the lips?
What is the nasal point called?
independent: Label every letter of Al-Falaq ayah 1 with its makhraj
Quiz in pairs with 20 letters
Record yourself reciting Al-Falaq and review
exit: Where is ف pronounced?
Name two letters with ghunnah.
lessons.homework: Learn the 17 makharij table and test yourself without looking.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: pre-labelled diagram and audio of each letter. Stretch: label a full ayah from another surah.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Sifat - the qualities of letters
lessons.title: Sifat 1: pairs of opposite qualities
objectives: Define sifat
Learn pairs of opposites
Describe a letter by its qualities

keywords.def: raising the back of the tongue
pressing the tongue against the roof of the mouth

teach.heading: Qualities as well as places
bullets: Both give a letter its identity
teach.note: Revisit the analogy of an instrument. Two letters from the same place may differ only in sifat, e.g. ط and ت. Ask: how are ط and ت different?

teach.heading: Opposite pairs
teach.note: Teach each pair. Itbaq letters: ص ض ط ظ. Isti'la letters: the seven heavy letters. Pupils demonstrate raising and lowering the tongue.

teach.heading: Strong and flowing
teach.note: Teach the phrases: أَجِدُكَ قَطَبْتَ for the eight strong letters; لِنْ عُمَر for the five middle letters. Pupils say a letter from each group and describe it.

teach.heading: Describe a letter
teach.note: Model the description of ط and ت. Then pupils describe ص and س. Link to why a wrong letter changes the word. This is not memorising a table; it is understanding the sound.

practice: Name the eight strong letters.
Which letters are pressed (itbaq)?
independent: Complete a qualities chart for 10 letters
Describe three letters orally to a partner
Find examples of each pair in Surat Al-Falaq
exit: What does isti'la mean?
What is the opposite of hams?
lessons.homework: Learn the memory phrases for hams and shiddah and test yourself.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: colour-coded qualities chart. Stretch: describe all letters of a word in terms of sifat.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Sifat - the qualities of letters
lessons.title: Sifat 2: special qualities
objectives: Know letters with unique qualities
Avoid a rolled raa
Apply qualities in recitation

keywords.def: whistling sound of ص ز س

teach.heading: The whistling letters
bullets: ص  ز  س have a whistling sound
Keep the sound clear, not harsh
teach.note: Contrast seen with thaa. Pupils say صِرَاطَ, زَيْتُون, سَبِّحْ. The whistling sound is part of the letter and must not be lost.

teach.heading: Qalqalah and leen
bullets: Qalqalah: ق ط ب ج د
Leen: soft waaw or yaa after fathah
Both show quality, not just rules
teach.note: Link rule to quality: qalqalah is an echo from the strong and voiced nature of those letters. Revise leen with خَوْفٍ and قُرَيْشٍ.

teach.heading: Sheen and Daad
bullets: ش - the sound spreads in the mouth
ض - the sound extends along the side of the tongue
teach.note: Say شَرِّ and الضَّالِّينَ. Pupils compare. Daad is taken slowly and gently. Arabic is nicknamed the language of Daad because of this letter.

teach.heading: Raa: not a roll
bullets: One quick touch of the tongue
teach.note: Contrast a rolled raa with a single tap. Revise the rules of tafkheem and tarqeeq. Take examples from the surahs: رَبِّ, رِحْلَةَ. Pupils record and listen.

practice: Which letters are whistling?
Is the raa rolled in Arabic recitation?
independent: Read eight words with special letters and say the quality
Listen to a reciter and identify examples
Record yourself reading a surah of your choice for a peer review
exit: Name a letter with safeer.
What is wrong with a rolled raa?
lessons.homework: Listen to a recording of Al-Fatihah by a reciter and write down three qualities you hear.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: audio clips and a labelled chart. Stretch: explain safeer and tafashshi to a classmate.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Sifat - the qualities of letters
lessons.title: Raa and laam: heavy or light?
objectives: State the rules for raa with a vowel and with a sukoon
Apply the rule for the laam of Allah
Read raa words correctly in surahs
starter: Is the raa in رَبِّ heavy or light?
Is the laam in بِسْمِ اللَّهِ heavy or light?

teach.heading: Raa with a vowel
teach.note: Revise from Year 3. Say each word, then say the vowel before deciding. Remember: in وِزْرَكَ the raa has a fathah, so it is heavy even though a kasrah is nearby.

teach.heading: Raa with a sukoon
teach.note: Rule of raa sakinah: look at the vowel before it. After kasrah it is light, unless a raised letter follows in the same word, as in مِرْصَادًا (78:21), where it is heavy. In فَارْغَب the raa follows a long aa so it is heavy.

teach.heading: The laam of Allah
teach.note: Revise: heavy after fathah or dammah, light after kasrah. All other laams are light. Pupils say the vowel and decide, then recite. Include الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ (light).

teach.heading: Apply it
teach.note: Pupils label each raa in Quraysh: قُرَيْشٍ (heavy), رِحْلَةَ (light), رَبَّ (heavy). Compare with a recording and discuss. Give feedback from the rubric.

practice: Is the raa in رِحْلَةَ heavy or light?
What decides the laam of Allah?
independent: Sort 12 words into heavy or light raa
Mark all raa and laam of Allah in Al-Ikhlas and Quraysh
Record yourself and listen for heavy and light
exit: State the rule for raa with a kasrah.
Give an example of a heavy laam of Allah.
lessons.homework: Find five words with raa in the mushaf and decide whether each is heavy or light.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: decision flow chart for raa. Stretch: explain the exception of raa sakinah before a raised letter.

lessons.title: Madd 1: the two families
objectives: Define madd asli and madd far'i
Identify the cause of madd
Sort madd by cause

keywords.def: secondary madd, longer because of a hamza or sukoon

starter: How many counts is natural madd?
Give a word with madd muttasil.

teach.heading: The two families
bullets: Far'i: caused by hamza or sukoon
teach.note: Draw a family tree with two branches. Explain that far'i builds on the natural madd and adds length for a reason. Ask: what are the two causes?

teach.heading: Cause: hamza
teach.note: Examples: السَّمَاءِ (muttasil), يَا أَيُّهَا (munfasil), آمَنُوا (badal). Pupils decide the cause in each. Revise the counts and remind that consistent length matters.

teach.heading: Cause: sukoon
bullets: Leen: waaw or yaa sakin, 2-6 when stopping
teach.note: Examples: الضَّالِّينَ (lazim), الْعَالَمِينَ stopped (arid), خَوْفٍ (leen). Pupils explain why each is longer than natural.

teach.heading: Sort and justify
teach.note: Use a sorting task with 12 words. Pupils justify each answer. Give feedback on reasoning, not only counts.

practice: Give the cause of madd lazim.
How many counts is badal?
independent: Sort 15 words on a table: type, cause, counts
Mark the madd in Al-Fatihah and Quraysh
Recite with accurate lengths
exit: Name the two causes of far'i madd.
Which madd is always six counts?
lessons.homework: Mark every madd in Surat Al-Fil and note its type and counts.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: flow chart for deciding madd type. Stretch: explain why lazim is longer than 'arid.

lessons.title: Madd 2: madd lazim in detail
objectives: Name the four types of madd lazim
Identify each type in the mushaf
Read each at six counts

keywords.def: in the name of a letter

starter: Give the counts for madd lazim.
Name a word with lazim from Al-Fatihah.

teach.heading: Four types
teach.note: Draw a 2x2 table: word or letter vs shaddah or sukoon. All four types are six counts. Ask: what do kalimi and harfi refer to?

teach.heading: Kalimi
bullets: Madd letter followed by shaddah or sukoon in the same word
teach.note: The mukhaffaf kalimi is rare and appears in آلْآنَ. Pupils read each example at six counts. Check the shaddah and sukoon.

teach.heading: Harfi
bullets: Letters at the start of some surahs
teach.note: Harfi occurs in the opening letters: pupils meet الم at the start of Al-Baqarah and ن at the start of Al-Qalam. The name of the letter is spelt out, e.g. لام and ميم, and that is why they are stretched. Present the principle; teacher demonstrates.

teach.heading: Practice
bullets: Do not rush into the next letter
teach.note: Pairs: one recites, the other counts with fingers. Provide feedback. Close with a short recitation of الضَّالِّينَ with steady six-count madd.

practice: How many counts is madd lazim?
What is the difference between kalimi and harfi?
independent: Label examples as kalimi/harfi, muthaqqal/mukhaffaf
Recite examples from the mushaf with six counts
Create a flow chart for deciding madd lazim type
exit: Name the four types of madd lazim.
Give an example of harfi.
lessons.homework: Find two examples of madd lazim in your mushaf and label their types.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: 2x2 table with examples. Stretch: find other letters at the start of surahs.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Qadr: reading and rules
objectives: Recite Al-Qadr accurately
Apply makharij, sifat and madd
Begin to memorise the surah
starter: Name the four types of madd lazim.

teach.heading: The surah
teach.note: Introduce the surah: Allah sent down the Qur'an on the Night of Decree. Chunk and echo. Rules: ghunnah in إِنَّا; ikhfa in أَنزَلْنَاهُ; laam qamariyyah in الْقَدْرِ.

teach.heading: Ayat 3-5
bullets: لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ
تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ
teach.note: Meaning: the Night of Decree is better than a thousand months; angels and the Spirit descend by their Lord's permission with every decree; peace it is until the rise of dawn. Chunk and echo.

teach.heading: Tajweed
teach.note: Check: tanween in خَيْرٌ meets meem: idgham with ghunnah. The noon of مِن meets kaaf in كُلِّ: ikhfa. The meem sakinah of رَبِّهِم meets meem: idgham shafawi. The madd in الْمَلَائِكَةُ is muttasil. Pupils label rules on a printed text.

teach.heading: Learn it
teach.note: Memorise ayat 1-2 now; 3 at home. Use chaining and test aloud. Praise accuracy of rules as well as memory.

practice: Recite Al-Qadr ayah 1.
Which rule is in خَيْرٌ مِّنْ؟
independent: Read Al-Qadr in pairs; label rules
Memorise ayat 1-2 with chaining
Recite individually
exit: What is better than a thousand months?
Name one tajweed rule in ayah 3.
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Qadr daily and learn ayat 1-3 by heart.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and text with rules highlighted. Stretch: learn the whole surah.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Qadr: meaning and reflection
objectives: Explain the main message of Al-Qadr
Use a simple method for tadabbur
Recite the whole surah from memory

keywords.def: reflecting deeply on the meaning of the Qur'an
the Night of Decree, in Ramadan

teach.heading: The message
bullets: The Qur'an was revealed on a blessed night
The night is better than a thousand months
teach.note: Ask the class what makes a time special. Explain that Allah has honoured this night, and that the sources indicate it is in Ramadan, in the last ten nights. Keep to what is established.

teach.heading: Questions to ask
bullets: What is said? The night is special
teach.note: Model a simple tadabbur method with these four questions. Use them on ayat 3-5. Ask for personal responses and acceptable answers.

teach.heading: Thinking about the Qur'an
bullets: كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوا آيَاتِهِ (38:29)
teach.note: Read these two ayat in meaning: do they not reflect upon the Qur'an; a blessed Book We sent down so they may ponder its verses. Link the two parts of the Qur'an's purpose: recite and think.

teach.heading: Putting it together
teach.note: Pupils recite Al-Qadr and complete a sentence: This surah teaches me ... so I will ... Share a few. Conclude with dua for the Night of Decree.

practice: Recite Al-Qadr.
Which ayah mentions the angels?
independent: Write answers to the four tadabbur questions
Recite Al-Qadr to a partner
Write a short reflection of 5 sentences on Al-Qadr
exit: What does the surah say about the Night of Decree?
Why do we reflect on the Qur'an?
lessons.homework: Write a half-page reflection on Al-Qadr and recite it every day.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sentence frames for tadabbur. Stretch: compare Al-Qadr with the ayah 2:185.

lessons.title: Memorisation technique and recital assessment
objectives: Describe a good memorisation routine
Revise Al-Qadr, Ad-Duha and Ash-Sharh
Complete a recital with the rubric
starter: Name the three parts of a revision plan.

teach.heading: A good routine
teach.note: Explain that memory improves through short, regular practice. Show a small weekly plan. Ask: what time of day is best for you?

teach.heading: Three layers
teach.note: Pupils plan a week using three layers. Show a sample. Notice that older surahs are revised weekly. Pupils may use a check-list.

teach.heading: Dealing with mistakes
bullets: Say the correct ayah five times
teach.note: Tell pupils that everyone forgets. Keep a list of difficult ayat. Do not give up. Encourage dua for strong memory and humility.

teach.heading: Recital
teach.note: Assess with the rubric from lesson 1. Provide one strength and one target. Compare with the baseline and celebrate progress.

practice: Recite Al-Qadr ayat 4-5.
Name one of your goals from September.
independent: Complete a revision plan for the next four weeks
Recite your chosen surah for the rubric
Write a reflection comparing baseline and now
exit: Name two layers of a revision plan.
What is one target for next term?
lessons.homework: Follow your revision plan daily for a week and note how it goes.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: revision planner with visual cues. Stretch: coach a partner in memorisation.
